# Stargazing Index

> Stargazing Index is a bilingual, data-driven guide for choosing stargazing destinations, months, observing sites, and astronomy gear. Its reviewed field guides, independent routes, and source-backed comparisons are supported by reproducible JSON data and clearly stated limitations.

The primary language is English. German versions use the same paths under `/de/`; each page declares reciprocal language alternates. Destination scores use historical climate normals and darkness data, not live weather. Astronomical sky simulations do not include local clouds, haze, terrain, buildings, vegetation, or measured on-site light pollution. Gear comparisons are editorial analyses of cited manufacturer specifications and do not claim hands-on testing unless explicitly stated.

## Choose the right source

- Use a destination guide to answer where to observe, which months have the strongest historical conditions, how access works, and which limitations affect the decision.
- Use a location tour for one concrete, source-backed evening plan at a named observing site.
- Use a short-trip guide to compare qualifying destinations from a specific origin city. A short-trip page can be deliberately excluded from indexing when no destination passes its evidence and distance gates.
- Use a gear guide for specification-based product comparisons. These guides do not publish live prices or claim unreported hands-on tests.
- Prefer the cited primary sources on each guide for current closures, bookings, opening times, protected-area rules, and manufacturer specifications.

## Editorial provenance

Stargazing Index is editorially managed by Schayan Yousefian. Every destination guide, location tour, and gear guide shows its responsible editor, review date, evidence, and material limitations. The latest review date represented in this index is 2026-08-31. Corrections can be submitted through the contact page. Affiliate relationships do not alter destination scores, rankings, or editorial conclusions.

## Gear guides

- [Beginner telescopes compared: three 130 mm paths](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/beginner-telescopes/): A source-backed comparison of three 130 mm f/5 Newtonian systems with different mounting and transport strategies.
- [8×42 binoculars compared for stargazing](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/binoculars/): A source-backed comparison of three waterproof 8×42 roof-prism binoculars for hand-held night-sky scanning and travel.
- [Red-light headlamps compared for stargazing](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/red-flashlights/): A source-backed comparison of three rechargeable headlamps with red modes, focused on night-safe controls rather than headline white-light output.
- [Berlebach observing chairs compared: Charon, Hydra II, and Nix II](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/observing-chairs/): A source-backed comparison of three folding wooden observing chairs, focused on usable seat range, adjustment mechanism, carried mass, packed length, and support at high positions.
- [Tripods compared for binoculars and small optics](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/tripods/): A source-backed comparison of three complete tripod-and-head kits for mounted binoculars, spotting scopes, and suitably light optical loads.
- [Travel star trackers compared: three routes into tracked nightscapes](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/star-trackers/): Compare three portable star trackers while accounting for the wedge, counterweight, ball head, and polar-alignment parts a complete field kit may need.
- [Dew heater controllers compared: manual simplicity or sensor-led control](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/dew-control/): Compare three 12 V dew-control systems, from two manual control groups to sensor-led channels, remote operation, and integrated power distribution.
- [Portable power stations compared for an astronomy field kit](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/portable-power/): Compare three 286–288 Wh LiFePO4 power stations by the USB, regulated 12 V, and AC outputs used by trackers, cameras, laptops, and dew heaters.
- [11–12.5 mm telescope eyepieces compared: field, eye relief, and mass](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/eyepieces/): Compare three 1.25-inch eyepieces around 11–12.5 mm and see how field of view, eye relief, waterproofing, and mass affect observing.
- [CLS, UHC-E, or UHC? Three visual filter passbands compared](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/astronomy-filters/): A source-backed comparison of three Astronomik visual filters that separates their published passbands, intended targets, aperture guidance, and real limits.
- [Three smartphone telescope adapters with very different alignment controls](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/smartphone-telescope-adapters/): A specification-led comparison of a three-axis metal-and-polymer clamp, a compact three-axis adapter, and a simple 1.25-inch eyepiece holder.
- [Three IMX585 colour cameras compared by cooling and control architecture](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/imx585-astronomy-cameras/): The shared Sony IMX585 sensor does not make these cameras equivalent: cooling, guide integration, storage, hubs, power and software define three different systems.
- [Large astronomy binoculars compared by field, eye relief and support demand](https://stargazingindex.com/en/gear/mounted-astronomy-binoculars/): This comparison treats high-power binoculars as an optical system plus support, not as oversized hand-held 8×42s.

## Machine-readable data

- [Dataset manifest](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/manifest.json): Dataset version, generation time, sources, counts, hashes, and checksums.
- [Destination index](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/destinations/index.json): Destination identifiers, countries, time zones, tags, and related observing sites.
- [Observation-site index](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/sites/index.json): Coordinates, elevation, access status, and source-backed access notes.
- [Editorial destination-guide index](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/editorial/destinations/index.json): Reviewed guide identifiers, word counts, source counts, and revision dates.
- [Editorial gear-guide index](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/gear/index.json): Bilingual specification comparisons with cited primary sources and dormant affiliate fields.
- [SEO registry](https://stargazingindex.com/data/stargazing/seo/registry.json): Canonicals, language alternates, descriptions, modification dates, and indexability decisions.
